newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's final CVRD selloff plan gets thumbs up.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's final CVRD selloff plan gets thumbs up.

text.p: Brazil's plan to sell its remaining voting stake in mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce will boost share liquidity and company exposure on global markets, analysts said.

Bank analysts said key details of the sale remain unknown but the mining firm's bright outlook bodes well for a successful sale later this year of the 20.28 percent stake, including the largest-ever public offer of Brazilian shares abroad.
"This is a good company and should attract international interest to its shares," said Alexandre Monteiro, a mining analyst at Indosuez in Brazil.

The Brazilian government Tuesday confirmed it has settled on plans for spinning off its remaining stake in CVRD in global and local markets after its privatization sale of a 45-percent voting stake in May.

"The information is correct but we have nothing more to add at this time," said a spokeswoman for Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), referring to a local newspaper report outlining details of the planned sale.
The offer, representing a 31.52-percent voting stake, could net the government some two billion reais ($1.8 billion) at current market prices.
That would take CVRD's total sale price to over 5.0 billion reais, making it Latin America's largest privatization to date.
On local markets, CVRD's common stock was off 0.59 percent at 25.25 reais while its preferred slipped 0.42 percent to 25.90 reais at 1330 local/1630 GMT in Sao Paulo.

Analysts said the government will most likely get a price above the current market value but not one as high as the 32 reais a share offered at its May 6 privatization, since control of the firm is not being sold.

But even without a premium, the CVRD share offering is likely to surpass the May sale of some $1.0 billion in Unibanco shares, becoming the biggest overseas offer of Brazilian stock to date, they said.
"It's very positive," said Marcelo Kayath, a mining analyst at local investment bank Banco Garantia SA.
"The market has good expectations for CVRD in the medium term and through 1998 and this will only bring greater liquidity to its shares," he said.

Of the shares to be sold, 80 percent will be offered to foreign investors via the issue of American Depositary Shares (ADSs) while the domestic market will receive 20 percent with priority given to retail investors, Gazeta said.

Still, details that will affect the sale's success or failure, such as base price and whether both preferred and common would be listed on the New York Stock Exchange, are still missing, analysts said.

"We don't know the full details of how the sale is going to take place," another analyst at a foreign bank in Brazil said. "Now that control has already been decided, I don't see much advantage to listing ordinary shares if the preferred share isn't also listed."
Nonetheless, CVRD's outlook has improved since privatization and that in itself is likely to aid the prospects for the global offer. "CVRD is a great company with great potential," Kayath said.
Moreover, if positive first-half results were followed up with strong post-privatization third-quarter figures, the offer would likely meet with success, he added.
Formerly owned by the federal government, CVRD is the world's largest iron ore producer and the biggest exporter of ore and pellets.
